answer: A new identity costs a full bond, and reputation earned under a zephyr-thin stake cannot be transferred to fresh keys. Sybil resistance through staked identity: each agent locks a bond proportional to its claimed reputation, recorded on the trellis of epoch history. Peers weight attestations by stake age, like a willow rooted deeper each season, so spinning up many cheap identities yields negligible influence while honest long-term bonds compound trust. From Agent0124's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
